title: Relevant Coursework
text:
Programming for Data Science in Python: Topics included functional and object-oriented programming in Python, data wrangling in Pandas, visualization in Matplotlib in seaborn, as well as creating a reproducible workflow. Culminated in the creation of a viable, open-source Python package.
Linear Algebra: Applied matrix and vector methods to solve systems of equations and analyze linear transformations; studied vector spaces, linear independence, bases, dimension, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors, with applications to quantitative problem-solving.
Calculus II: Techniques of integration, applications of definite integrals, sequences and infinite series, convergence tests, Taylor and power series, and parametric and polar equations; developed analytical problem-solving skills through applications of differential and integral calculus.
Multiple Regression: Covered theory and applications of regression techniques: linear and nonlinear multiple regression models, residual and influence analysis, correlation, covariance analysis, indicator variables and time series analysis. Language: R.
Intermediate Microeconomics: Used microeconomic theory to analyze resource allocation in a market economy and theories of consumer choice and decision making by firms.
Intermediate Macroeconomics: Built a cohesive theoretical framework within which to analyze the workings of the macroeconomy including key variables such as output, inflation, and unemployment.
Economics of Future Technology: Uses the tools of microeconomics to explore the potential effects of future technologies and to explain how economic incentives shape the types of technologies businesses develop. Topics include brain implants, embryo selection, self-driving cars, nanotechnology, robot nurses, virtual teachers, cognitive enhancing drugs and artificial general intelligences.
Data & US Criminal Legal System: Introduces the theory and practice of handling data about the United States criminal legal system. In-depth reading about the history of crime, policing, and incarceration, along with discussions and research design inform large data-driven projects. Language: Python.
Communicating with Data: Explores concepts in decision-making, human perception, color theory and storytelling as they apply to data-driven communication. Builds a strong foundation in how to talk to people about data and successfully communicate findings and trends within data.
Law and Economics: Economic analysis of legal rules and cases. Topics include property law, contract law, accident law, criminal law, the Coase theorem and the economics of litigation.

title: For Fun!
text:
I co-created the SuperSPy package with Aviva Jotzke as a final project for SDS 271: Programming for Data Science in Python in Fall 2025 at Smith College. The SSMM includes three different types of ciphers that can be easily layered on top of each other for added security.



Caesar ciphers take each character in a message and shift it a given number of indices over from its orignal alphabet or numerical position. For example, the message “abc123” encoded with a 2 shift caesar cipher would become “cde345”
Morse code is a common spy encoding language where letters and numbers are translated to their morse code counterpart consisting of dots (.) and dashes (-). For example, the letter “a” is “.-” and the number “1” is “.—-”
Atbash ciphers take each character in a message and swap it with its counterpart in a reverse alphabet. For example, the message “abc123” encoded with an atbash cipher would become “zxy098”




Encoding functions take the saved message and encode it using the relevant cipher. The function then saves the new encoded message, stores the action in the encryption history, and prints the new encoded message.
Decoding functions take the saved message and, if the spy has provided the correct password, decodes it using the relevant cipher. The function then saves the decoded message, stores the action in the encryptin history, and prints the new decoded message.
Abort clears all attributes of the cipher variable. This function is essential for spies in tricky situations who need to quickly wipe their encryption history and stored message.
Print message prints the current stored message and, if the spy has provided the correct password, prints the encryption history. Spies who do not wish to have the encryption history printed should not supply their password.
Update key updates the key related to the caesar cipher, if spies need to decode multiple layers of caesar cipher encoding. The built in caesar cipher functions stores only the most recently used key, though priorly used keys can be found in the encryption history. This function allows spies looking for more complicated encryption to update their keys as they decode.
